label: def:double-slit-q-phase
title: $q$-deformed path phase
html:
Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with substrate parameter q \in k^{\times} (substrate parameter). Let \gamma_i (i = 1,2) be two paths through slits of width a separated by distance d.

The q-deformed path phase along \gamma_i is

  \Phi_q^{(i)}(y)
  =  \frac{1}{\hbar_q}\!\int_{\gamma_i}\! d_q\psi
  =  q^{-1}\Phi_{\mathrm{geom}}^{(i)}(y)
        +  (1 - q^{-1})\Phi_{\mathrm{Reeb}}^{(i)}(y).

The terms are:

  • \Phi_{\mathrm{geom}}^{(i)} = (2\pi/\lambda)\ell_i(y): The geometric phase.
  • \Phi_{\mathrm{Reeb}}^{(i)} = \int_{\gamma_i} \iota_\xi\varTheta: The Reeb phase (Reeb derivation).
  • \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}: The quantum Planck constant.

This decomposition stems from the q-exterior derivative d_q = q^{-1}d + (1 - q^{-1})\pi_V \circ d.

The q-deformed phase difference is

  \Delta\Phi_q(y)
  =  \Phi_q^{(1)}(y) - \Phi_q^{(2)}(y)
  =  q^{-1}\frac{2\pi d\sin\theta}{\lambda}
        +  (1 - q^{-1})\Delta\phi_\xi(y).

Here \theta is the scattering angle and \Delta\phi_\xi(y) is the Reeb phase mismatch. At q = 1, the Reeb term vanishes.
